description.narrative: On 20 January 2020 (6 Magh 2076 B.S), the Government of Nepal through its cabinet approved the National Occupational Safety and Health Policy presented by the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Security. The policy is in line with Occupational Safety and Health Convention, 1981 (No. 155), and particularly provides authorities to provincial and local governments to monitor OSH standards at workplaces. The ILO reviewed and provided inputs to the draft National Occupational Safety and Health Policy as well as facilitated consultation meetings between government and social partners. The ILO also provided technical advice in the completion of a gap analysis on existing policies and laws.

description.narrative: • Through the ILO employment and livelihoods support programme, 1,000 former forced labour families (Haliyas - 700 and Haruwa-Charuwas - 300) increased their income, with 70 per cent of the Haliyas trained are either self-employed or work for a wage. • Total 269 (F: 122; M:147) Municipal Council members including Mayors, Deputy Mayors, Ward Chairpersons, Ward representatives Elected representatives and local Government officials were reached by WIF program to recognize and value women's work and enable access to decent work opportunities for women at local level thereby contributing to reducing risks of trafficking and labour exploitation. • Strengthened capacity of the ILO social partners for the promotion of ratification of the ILO Forced Labour Protocol 2014. • ILO Bridge Project, in partnership with a training provider, organised livelihoods training to 700 former bonded labourers (Haliyas) in Sudurpakchhim (Bajura and Kanchanpur districts) and Karnali province (Surkhet district). Additional 300 Haliyas and Haruwa Charuwas will be provided livelihood training in Karnali Province (Jajarkot) and Province 2 (Siraha and Saptari Districts). By 2021, all together 1,000 family members of the ex-bonded labourers will receive skill training. • ILO WIF programme with its three partners in four districts organised workshops for local level leaders in 2020 advocating for women's rights to access decent work at local level (municipality level). • Provided technical assistance to develop training manual on identifying forced labour cases tested and incorporated forced labour indicators into the labour inspection system of the federal government. A training involving ILO constitutes organised using the training manual.
